question: Who among the following established its factory in Petapuli on the North Coromandel Coast in 1606? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Spanish East India Company
Dutch East India Company
German East India Company
Danish East India Company
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dutch East India Company

Explanation:
The Dutch East India Company (VOC) established its factory at Petapuli (present-day Andhra Pradesh) on the North Coromandel Coast in 1606. This marks the early Dutch presence in India. The Dutch set up multiple factories in India to control the spice trade. The Petapuli factory was mainly used for textile and spice trading. The Dutch East India Company was founded in 1602 and was one of the most powerful trading companies in the 17th century.

question:
Which factor has contributed most to the depletion of high-grade mineral ores in India over recent decades?
(RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Increased export of unprocessed minerals
Selective mining of rich ores
Limited foreign investment in mining
Overdependence on coal-based industries
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Selective mining of rich ores

Explanation:
The primary factor contributing to the depletion of high-grade mineral ores in India over recent decades is selective mining of rich ores. Mining companies, driven by profit maximization, extract only high-grade ores, leaving behind low-grade ones, leading to rapid exhaustion of quality reserves. Inefficient mining techniques and poor regulatory compliance have worsened the situation. As a result, the availability of high-grade iron ore, bauxite, and other minerals has decreased, increasing import dependence and hindering sustainable resource management.

question:
Which of the following options correctly explains why the eastern coastal plains of India are wider and more deltaic than the western coastal plains?
(RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 2)
options: Eastern rivers flow over steep gradients
Eastern rivers form large deltas due to gentle slopes
Eastern plains have more tectonic uplift
Eastern plains receive less tidal influence
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Eastern rivers form large deltas due to gentle slopes

Explanation:
The eastern coastal plains of India are wider and more deltaic than the western coastal plains because the eastern rivers (e.g., Ganga, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) flow over gentle slopes. Due to the gentle gradient, these rivers deposit large amounts of sediment at their mouths, forming extensive deltas. In contrast, the western coastal plains are narrow because the Western Ghats run close to the west coast, and the rivers are short with steep gradients, preventing delta formation. Rivers like Narmada and Tapi flow through rift valleys and form estuaries instead of deltas. Tectonic uplift and tidal influence are not primary reasons for this difference.

☛ Why no deltas form on the west coast? → Short rivers with steep gradients
☛ Which is the largest lake on the east coast? → Chilika Lake

question: Which of the following features distinguishes the Purvanchal hills from the rest of the Himalayan mountain system? (RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 2)
options: They stretch in a convex arc along the eastern frontier
They include the Aravalli and Satpura hill groups
They are snow-covered throughout the year
They form the highest peaks of the Zanskar range
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is They stretch in a convex arc along the eastern frontier

Explanation:
The Purvanchal hills are the eastern extension of the Himalayan mountain system, located along India's eastern frontier. They are distinguished from the rest of the Himalayas by their convex arc shape. Unlike the main Himalayan ranges, these hills are relatively low in altitude and are not snow-covered throughout the year. The Purvanchal includes hill groups like Patkai, Naga, Manipur, Mizo, Tripura, Mikir, and Garo-Khasi-Jaintia. In contrast, the Aravalli and Satpura ranges belong to the Peninsular India, and the Zanskar range is part of the Central Himalayas. This unique orientation and composition set the Purvanchal apart.

Explanation:
पूर्वांचल की पहाड़ियाँ हिमालय पर्वत प्रणाली का पूर्वी विस्तार हैं, जो भारत की पूर्वी सीमा पर स्थित हैं। ये पहाड़ियाँ एक उत्तल चाप के आकार में फैली हुई हैं, जो इन्हें शेष हिमालय से अलग करता है। हिमालय के अन्य भागों की तुलना में पूर्वांचल की पहाड़ियाँ अपेक्षाकृत नीची हैं और इनमें बर्फ नहीं जमती। इनमें पटकोई, नागा, मणिपुर, मिजो, त्रिपुरा, मिकिर और गारो-खासी-जयंतिया जैसी पहाड़ियाँ शामिल हैं। अरावली और सतपुड़ा पहाड़ियाँ प्रायद्वीपीय भारत का हिस्सा हैं, जबकि ज़ांस्कर श्रृंखला मध्य हिमालय का भाग है।

question: Which forest type in India is known for its year-round green canopy due to no fixed period of leaf shedding? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Montane pine forests
Tropical thorn forests
Tropical evergreen forests
Dry deciduous forests
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tropical evergreen forests

Explanation:
Tropical evergreen forests in India are known for their year-round green canopy as they have no fixed period of leaf shedding. These forests thrive in warm and humid climates with annual rainfall exceeding 200 cm and temperatures between 20-25°C. They are primarily found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the Western Ghats, and parts of northeastern India. The dense multi-layered canopy allows little sunlight to reach the ground. Important tree species include rosewood, teak, and mahogany. Unlike other options, montane pine forests occur in mountainous regions, tropical thorn forests in arid areas, and dry deciduous forests shed leaves during the dry season.

☛ Temperature range → 20°C - 25°C
☛ Major tree species → Rosewood, Teak, Mahogany
☛ Largest evergreen forest area → Western Ghats

question: Which of the following regions would you expect has the highest population density based on geographic factors? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Ganga River basin in India
Canadian Arctic tundra
Sahara Desert in Africa
Amazon rainforest in Brazil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ganga River basin in India

Explanation:
The Ganga River basin is highly favorable for agriculture due to fertile alluvial soil, adequate rainfall, and flat terrain. The extensive river network facilitates irrigation and abundant water resources. The temperate climate is ideal for human habitation. Historically, this region has been the center of civilizations. In contrast, the Canadian Arctic tundra is covered with extreme cold and ice; the Sahara Desert is extremely arid; and the Amazon rainforest is unsuitable for dense population due to dense forest and high humidity.

question: How does higher soil moisture retention in black soils influence cropping intensity in regions like Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: It supports multiple cropping cycles by sustaining moisture across seasons
It encourages plantation crops over food grains due to deep root support
It limits cropping to a single season to prevent waterlogging
It reduces the need for crop rotation due to stable nutrient levels
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It limits cropping to a single season to prevent waterlogging

Explanation:
Black soils have high moisture retention capacity due to their clayey nature (mainly montmorillonite). This causes excessive water retention after the monsoon season. If farmers try to grow a second crop (e.g., rabi) after kharif, the high soil moisture leads to waterlogging, which damages roots and reduces oxygen availability. To avoid this, cropping intensity is limited to a single season, typically kharif, where crops like cotton, sugarcane, and soybean are grown. Thus, the high moisture retention ability of black soils reduces the number of crop cycles per year, making cropping intensity low. This is a key reason for the practice of keeping land fallow in rabi season in black soil regions of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Reason for high moisture retention in black soil → Presence of montmorillonite clay.
☛ Major crop of black soil → Cotton, hence called 'regur soil' or 'cotton soil'.
☛ States with black soil → Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh.
☛ Effect of waterlogging on crops → Roots lack oxygen, leading to plant death.
☛ Other feature of black soil → Self-ploughing ability as it swells when wet and shrinks when dry.

question: Which of the following was NOT an excavated site of the Banas culture? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Gilund
Bagor
Nagda
Ahar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nagda

Explanation:
The Banas culture, also known as the Ahar culture, was a Chalcolithic culture that flourished in the Banas river region of Rajasthan. Its major excavated sites include Ahar, Gilund, and Bagor. In contrast, Nagda is an archaeological site in Madhya Pradesh associated with the Malwa culture. The Banas culture is characterized by red and black pottery, copper objects, and an agricultural lifestyle. Excavations at Nagda were conducted in 1955-56, revealing a significant center of the Malwa culture. Therefore, Nagda was not an excavated site of the Banas culture.

question: Which of the following factors causes Ooty to have cooler summers than Coimbatore, even though both are located at nearly the same latitude? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Ooty is influenced by cold desert winds from the north
Coimbatore receives less solar radiation during the year
Ooty is located closer to the sea, while Coimbatore is inland
Ooty is situated at a higher altitude, leading to lower temperatures
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ooty is situated at a higher altitude, leading to lower temperatures

Explanation:
Ooty and Coimbatore are located at nearly the same latitude, yet Ooty experiences cooler summers due to difference in altitude. Ooty is situated at an elevation of about 2240 meters above sea level, while Coimbatore is at about 432 meters. As altitude increases, temperature decreases (approximately 6.5°C per 1000 meters), known as the lapse rate. This makes Ooty's average temperature significantly lower than Coimbatore's. Other options are incorrect: Ooty is not influenced by cold desert winds from the north; Coimbatore does not receive less solar radiation; and Ooty is not closer to the sea but is an inland hill station.

question: Which of the following best explains the difference between weather and climate? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Weather and climate mean exactly the same phenomenon
Weather refers to long-term trends; climate refers to short-term changes
Weather is permanent in nature; climate is temporary in nature
Weather refers to short-term changes; climate refers to long-term patterns
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Weather refers to short-term changes; climate refers to long-term patterns

Explanation:
Weather describes the atmospheric conditions (temperature, humidity, precipitation, wind) at a specific place over a short period (minutes, hours, or days). It is short-term and changes rapidly. Climate represents the average weather patterns and trends in a region over a long period (typically 30 years or more). It is stable and long-term. For instance, rain on a particular day is weather, while average annual rainfall of 100 cm in a region is a climate indicator. Thus, weather captures short-term variations, whereas climate reflects long-term averages.

It is one of the earliest structural temples in South India and exemplifies the transition from rock-cut to structural architecture.

question: What is the primary reason for the intensification of the monsoon trough over North India by the end of May? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Shift in wind patterns
Increase in atmospheric pressure
High temperature in the region
Decrease in humidity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is High temperature in the region

Explanation:
By the end of May, the landmass over North India becomes extremely hot due to the vertical rays of the sun. This high temperature strengthens the thermal low-pressure area, which pulls the monsoon trough northward and intensifies it. The temperature gradient between the hot land and the relatively cooler sea activates the trough, accelerating the monsoon's progress. Other options like shift in wind patterns or increase in pressure are secondary factors, while decrease in humidity reduces intensity.

question: Which of the following irrigation methods leads to the least wastage of water? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 2)
options: Furrow irrigation
Flood irrigation
Drip irrigation
Sprinkler irrigation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Drip irrigation

Explanation:
Drip irrigation is an efficient irrigation method where water is delivered directly to the plant roots drop by drop. This minimizes evaporation and runoff, leading to the least wastage of water. In contrast, flood irrigation involves flooding the entire field, causing significant water loss through evaporation and percolation. Furrow irrigation, where water flows in channels, also results in some wastage. Sprinkler irrigation sprays water into the air, leading to evaporation losses. Drip irrigation achieves water use efficiency of over 90%, while other methods range from 50-70%. It is especially beneficial in arid and water-scarce regions, as it reduces water consumption and improves crop yield.

question: What type of agriculture is still widely practiced in India despite modern agricultural changes? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Subsistence Agriculture
Organic Agriculture
Commercial Agriculture
Plantation Agriculture
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Subsistence Agriculture

Explanation:
Despite modern agricultural changes, Subsistence Agriculture is still widely practiced in India. In this method, farmers grow crops to meet the needs of themselves and their families. It involves traditional techniques such as plowing with bullocks and reliance on rainfall for irrigation. Most small and marginal farmers practice subsistence agriculture, especially in rural areas. About 60-70% of farmers in India are small and marginal, owning less than 2 hectares of land. Despite the adoption of modern technologies and high-yielding varieties, subsistence agriculture remains prevalent due to dependence on monsoons and limited market access. It is the oldest form of agriculture and still forms the backbone of Indian agriculture.

question: Sonora-64 and Lerma Rojo are high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of which crop introduced during the Green Revolution in India? (RRB JE (19/02/2026) Shift 1)
options: Rice
Barley
Wheat
Maize
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Wheat

Explanation:
Sonora-64 and Lerma Rojo are high-yielding varieties of wheat introduced during the Green Revolution in India in the 1960s. Developed by Dr. Norman Borlaug, these semi-dwarf varieties were highly responsive to fertilizers and irrigation, leading to a dramatic increase in wheat production. In India, their adoption boosted wheat output from 12 million tonnes in 1965 to 20 million tonnes by 1970. These Mexican varieties were first cultivated in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh, transforming India from a food-deficient nation to a self-sufficient one.
